Is Your Kid Ready for Their First Phone? A Cynical Checklist for the Modern Parent

The dreaded “When can I get my own phone?” moment feels inevitable—one minute you’re untangling shoelaces, the next they’re demanding a portal to a world of predators, bullies, and misinformation. Spoiler: there’s no magical age. Readiness is as personal as the age you learned to walk.

### Ditch the Age‑Based Rulebook. Use a Checklist.

Responsibility in the real world:
Returns library books on time.
Feeds the pet without a daily reminder.
Keeps track of sports gear or school supplies.
Completes chores consistently.

Maturity around screens:
Self‑regulates gaming when the “off‑screen” bell rings.
Doesn’t melt down when the device is unplugged.
Knows when “I’m done” feels genuine, not forced.

Communication chops:
Articulates problems instead of throwing tantrums.
Asks thoughtful questions rather than demanding.
Expresses frustration without turning the house into a war zone.

Basic digital literacy:
Understands that anything posted online is forever.
Knows personal info is not public property.
Recognizes the red flag of strangers offering gifts.

Functional necessity:
If coordination of activities, health‑related contact, or genuine peer‑to‑peer communication is required—and it isn’t just “because everyone else has one”—the case for a device strengthens.

### Red Flags: When to Hit Pause

❌ Chronic irresponsibility—lost items, forgotten appointments, habitual lying.
❌ Emotional volatility—meltdowns over minor setbacks, poor impulse control.
❌ Ignorance of privacy basics—no grasp of why certain content is off‑limits.
